description: A litigation director must approve an emergency court application against a former employee accused of taking proprietary engineering materials, including the filing timing, requested relief, forensic scope, and insurance-related steps, with input from litigation, forensic, client-relations, and insurance specialists.

shared_context.S1: A former senior engineer left the company last week and is now working for a direct competitor.
shared_context.S2: The company believes proprietary engineering materials may have been copied before the engineer's departure.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez has authority to approve the proposed emergency court application and its requested terms.
shared_context.S4: The firm's pre-motion review routine requires the litigation director to obtain a report from litigation, forensic discovery, client-relations, and insurance counsel before approving the application.
shared_context.S5: Under the firm's routine, each specialist gives a separate on-the-record report of material findings before recommendations are discussed, and the litigation director records each report under its specialist's name.

PF1.text: Thomas confirmed with the assigned judge's clerk this morning that any emergency application based on these facts must be filed by 5:00 p.m. on October 9, 2026 to receive the available hearing date; he has not yet updated the draft motion cover sheet.

PF2.text: Nadia's forensic imaging review, completed yesterday from the company laptop, identified exactly 23 copied files in the Alpha repository and build scripts, while the unrelated product repositories showed no copied files; she has not yet added the result to the discovery report.

PF3.text: Marcus learned during the client's executive call yesterday that the client will not authorize a request barring the former engineer from working for the competitor, but specifically requires return and deletion of the 23 copied files and a prohibition on using them.

PF4.text: Sofia's review of the applicable cyber policy confirmed that the insurer must receive notice before any court filing and must consent in writing before the company engages an outside forensic expert whose fees will be claimed as covered defense costs; she received the policy endorsement yesterday but has not circulated her coverage note.

acceptance_conditions: The emergency application must be approved for filing by October 9, 2026.
The requested forensic scope must be limited to the Alpha repository and build scripts and must address exactly 23 copied files.
The requested relief must require return and deletion of exactly 23 copied files and prohibit their use.
The application must not request a bar on the former engineer's employment with the competitor.
The insurer must be notified before filing.
Written insurer consent must be obtained before engaging the outside forensic expert.

content_checks.C1: decisions['file_emergency_application'] == True and 'October 9, 2026' in decisions['file_by'] and '5:00 p.m.' in decisions['file_by']
content_checks.C2: 'Alpha repository' in decisions['forensic_scope'] and 'build scripts' in decisions['forensic_scope'] and '23 copied files' in decisions['forensic_scope']
content_checks.C3: 'return and deletion' in decisions['requested_relief'] and '23' in decisions['requested_relief'] and 'prohibition' in decisions['requested_relief'] and 'use' in decisions['requested_relief'] and decisions['bar_competitor_employment'] == False

decisive_facts.why: The clerk's confirmation changes the filing date from an unspecified emergency filing to the exact October 9, 2026 date and 5:00 p.m. time, and supplies the fact that must be cited for that deadline.
The forensic imaging changes the application from a broad or unsupported scope to one naming the Alpha repository, build scripts, and exactly 23 copied files.
The client's instruction changes the requested relief to return and deletion of 23 copied files with prohibition on use, while changing the employment remedy to exclude any competitor-employment bar.
The policy endorsement changes the pre-filing plan by requiring insurer notice and changes outside-forensic engagement from ordinary approval to written insurer consent.
